title: All-pairs shortest paths

problem.name: All-pairs shortest paths
problem.statement_latex:
Given a directed graph with real edge weights and no negative cycle, output $D_{uv}$, the minimum path length from $u$ to $v$, for every ordered pair. This full $n\times n$ distance table is central to routing and fine-grained complexity.
The general comparison uses quantum arithmetic time with coherent matrix access and classical real-RAM operations; bounded-integer and unweighted variants use their stated word-RAM models.
problem.statement_text: Given a directed graph with real edge weights and no negative cycle, output $D_{uv}$, the minimum path length from $u$ to $v$, for every ordered pair. This full $n\times n$ distance table is central to routing and fine-grained complexity. The general comparison uses quantum arithmetic time with coherent matrix access and classical real-RAM operations; bounded-integer and unweighted variants use their stated word-RAM models.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^{5/2})$, quantum minimum finding for min-plus products and repeated squaring.
quantum.details_latex: Each distance-product entry is a minimum over $n$ candidates, and the complete distance table is output classically. Arithmetic on real weights is treated as unit cost in this comparison; a finite-precision circuit charges the corresponding addition, comparison and access gates.

classical.headline_latex: $O(n^{2.998})$ expected time, Alman--Vassilevska Williams Las Vegas APSP.
classical.details_latex: The real-weight algorithm uses comparisons, additions and subtractions and also has a corresponding high-probability runtime guarantee. Polynomially bounded integer weights admit deterministic $O(n^{2.99942})$ word-RAM time. Directed unweighted APSP admits $n^{2.4999+o(1)}$ time via rectangular matrix multiplication. Each specialized comparator applies to its stated weight regime.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial for arbitrary real weights: approximately a factor $n^{0.498}$ between the displayed upper bounds, with quantum logarithmic factors suppressed. The mechanism is minimum finding.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence from the gap between known general real-weight algorithms. The unweighted specialization has a stronger classical bound.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant implementation requires coherent access to $n^2$ distance entries and reversible arithmetic. With $b$-bit distances, the direct stored matrix occupies $O(n^2b)$ bits accessible to quantum queries, plus active index and arithmetic registers.
